comments.note: AC5 grep for https?:// produces a false positive on basic_selectors.php because https://example.com appears inside the heredoc fixture string. No network-making function is present. Future AC wording could specify 'no calls to file_get_html, file_get_contents, curl, or fsockopen' to avoid ambiguity.

extract_text.php full-document plaintext output includes heavy whitespace from the heredoc indentation (spaces between words in the title, paragraphs, etc.). This is correct Parser behaviour — text() preserves inter-node whitespace. The example uses trim() on sections so the output is acceptable for a demo, but a reader unfamiliar with the engine may be surprised. A brief inline comment in the file explaining this behaviour would improve the pedagogical value.

No null-guard on indexed find() calls (e.g., $html->find('h1#main-title', 0)->plaintext). Fine for hardcoded fixtures, but worth noting for readers who may adapt these patterns to real-world HTML where the element may be absent.

summary: All three WP-002 files pass code review across all four dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context).

Three Fix-Forward comment additions applied directly (non-behavioral): null-return annotation on indexed find() in basic_selectors.php; boolean-attribute semantics comment in advanced_selectors.php; whitespace-preservation explanation in extract_text.php.
One Documentation-Forward item tagged: the api-surface.md plaintext property entry could document whitespace-preservation behavior to avoid reader surprise.

comments.note: basic_selectors.php: added inline comment `// returns null if the element is absent` after the `find('h1#main-title', 0)` call. Alerts readers adapting the pattern to real-world HTML where elements may be missing.

advanced_selectors.php: added comment explaining that boolean attributes return true when present, false when absent. Clarifies why the truthy ternary `$cb->checked ? 'checked' : 'unchecked'` is semantically correct, which is non-obvious without reading Node::__get().

extract_text.php: added comment `// plaintext preserves inter-node whitespace from the source; trim() gives cleaner CLI output` before the full-document echo. Explains the extra-whitespace behaviour that QA flagged as potentially surprising.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md entry for the `plaintext` property (and/or the `text()` method) should document that inter-node whitespace is preserved in the output. Callers working with indented heredoc fixtures or real-world HTML will encounter unexpectedly padded strings without this note.
